flashcard_questions.q: The distance and framing of the camera relative to the subject, determining how much of the scene is visible in the frame. Examples include close-up, medium shot and long shot.
The position of the camera relative to the subject's height, such as high angle (looking down), low angle (looking up) or eye level.
The physical movement of the camera during filming, such as panning (horizontal rotation), tilting (vertical rotation), tracking (moving alongside the subject), or zooming (changing focal length).

flashcard_questions.a: It feels shaky and raw, which adds urgency, chaos or realism.
flashcard_questions.q: What effect does a handheld shot have on the audience?
